ledger.claim: The three core artifacts describe one and the same trip: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00537, and the gps_trace's first fix (2026-09-25T21:06:40+08:00) aligns with the trip_record's started_at. The rider's initial identification burden under POL-RD-08 is therefore discharged and the debate proceeds on this trip's own record.

The gps_trace is clean: 115 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix interval of 0 s, so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and no corroboration question arises. On that trace the vehicle travelled 4.59 km, and under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs the threshold test - the trip_record's rounded 4.6 km may not be cited for it.

Concession, and the rider does not stretch it: on the trace figure the excess over the booked optimal of 4.5 km is 0.09 km, or 2.00% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH establishment tests to pass - more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of optimal - and neither is met. No route deviation is established on this trip, and for that reason the rider does not press a POL-RD-02 distance-and-time recomputation.

The rider's grievance is the fare level, not the road: the 28.45 charged is the metered fare for 4.6 km and 19 min (base 3.80 + distance 3.45 + time 5.32 = 12.57) carried by the 2.2x surge recorded on fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, giving 27.654, plus the 0.80 platform fee. The rider acknowledges that POL-RD-02 itself reads the surge multiplier from that field and feeds it into its arithmetic, so a lawfully recorded surge is not a ground of refund under this policy, and the rider does not ask the tribunal to rewrite the fare model or award a remedy the policy does not provide.

There is no billing-integrity correction to make under POL-RD-09 either: the fare_breakdown carries an airport_surcharge of 0.00 and an ERP/toll total of 0.00 with an empty erp_gantries list, so no phantom gantry line and no wrongly applied airport surcharge exists to refund as a standalone correction. The rider raises this so the record is complete, not to manufacture a line the ledger does not contain.

No traffic_advisory covers this trip window: EV-ADVIS-00537-01 carries admissibility status MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) and no payload. I disclose that impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. Its consequence is that there is nothing on the record that could exculpate any excess under POL-RD-03, and the driver's assertion that he drove the normal route is measured against the trace alone.

The rider's profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the POL-RD-08 heightened-corroboration condition - four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated - does not apply, and this claim is not subject to any corroboration requirement beyond the gps_trace. These are the exact trailing-window fields POL-RD-08 names, cited for that test alone under POL-GEN-01.

The governing distance measurement on this trip is the gps_trace polyline, and it records 4.59 km against a booked optimal route of 4.5 km. That is an excess of 0.09 km — 2.0% of optimal. Neither limb of the POL-RD-01 establishment test is met: the excess is not greater than 20% of optimal and it is not greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. Both tests must pass for a deviation to exist, so no route deviation is established on this trip and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises it.

The two distance fields agree and neither supports the rider. The trip_record carries a rounded 4.6 km actual distance — a convenience copy that POL-RD-01 says may not be cited for the threshold test — and even taking it, the excess over the 4.5 km optimal is 0.1 km, still an order of magnitude short of the 0.8 km absolute gate. On either field the deviation fails, and the trace figure governs in any event.

What the rider is actually complaining about is price, not route: the difference between a noon trip and this 9 pm trip. The fare_breakdown records a surge_multiplier of 2.2 and a surge uplift of SGD 15.08, and the POL-RD-02 commentary fixes that field's home as fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and nowhere else. Surge on a METERED fare explains the total the rider objects to; it is not a detour, and the distance actually driven is the optimal distance.

POL-RD-02's recomputation — and therefore any arithmetic refund — runs only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01'. Since establishment fails on this trip's own trace, the recomputation route is closed and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider. The present charge stands and the correct outcome is NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03: on this rider-filed dispute it leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they are.

No adjustment, exoneration or billing correction changes the result. The fare_breakdown itemises no ERP gantries at all and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom or unmatched line to refund, and there is no off-route pass-through to correct. The rider's remedy list is empty because there is no defect on the ledger.

The trace that decides this case is clean, so nothing needs corroborating and no escalation is engaged. It carries 100% coverage, 115 fixes at a 10-second cadence, an empty gaps list and a 0-second maximum gap, with the reported sampling interval equal to the expected interval. POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) do not fire, POL-RD-10(3) is not triggered, and the record is fully able to answer the question posed.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. Limb (a) is satisfied — trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all read TRP-00537 — but limb (b) fails on the rider's own evidence, because the measured excess is 0.09 km, far below threshold. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, no exculpatory clause is needed, and the claim is discarded for want of the threshold fact.

The bundle's traffic advisory is MISSING: I disclose that EV-ADVIS-00537-01 has weight_multiplier 0.0 and carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and it can carry no fact for either side. The driver asserts no queue, closure or external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 is not invoked and POL-RD-13's advisory comparison is not engaged. The absence of an advisory no party has cited is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it, and it cannot manufacture a POL-RD-10(5) escalation the driver has not raised.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this dispute is about the fare you paid, but the policy only moves money on a route-deviation or billing-integrity defect, and neither exists on this record.

Route: the gps_trace (EV-GPS-00537) governs the threshold test and records 4.59 km against the booked optimal route of 4.5 km on the trip_record (EV-TRIP-00537). That is an excess of 0.09 km — 2.00% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to pass BOTH gates, more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20% of optimal; neither passes. No route deviation is established. The trip_record's rounded 4.6 km is a convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the test, and even taken it would still fail by an order of magnitude. The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)–(c): 115 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, 0-second maximum interval — so nothing needs corroborating and no escalation under POL-RD-10(3) arises.

Fare: because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's recomputation does not run at all. I note for transparency what it would have produced had it run — a recomputed fare of 23.3610 against the charged 28.45, a 5.10 refund — but its trigger is absent, so no distance-or-time refund is available. The figure you are objecting to is the 2.2x surge recorded on fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (EV-FARE-00537), which adds a surge uplift of 15.08 to this trip and accounts for the 28.45 total. Surge is a lawful part of a METERED fare under this policy, POL-RD-02 itself reads the multiplier from that field, and no clause provides a refund for a lawfully recorded surge. The driver's statement that surge was on is consistent with the ledger.

Billing integrity: the fare_breakdown carries no ERP gantry, no toll and no airport surcharge (all 0.00 with an empty gantry list), so there is no phantom line and nothing for POL-RD-09(4) to refund. No amendment of pickup or dropoff was made, and the chat log is empty, so no rider-requested detour arises.

I also record that the bundle's traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00537-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT). No party asserted an external traffic cause, so it carries no fact for either side; the absence is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction, and it neither exonerates any excess nor triggers an escalation. Confidence in this ruling rests on the gps_trace and the trip_record, both at weight 1.0, and is therefore not capped below the floor. The charge of 28.45 stands, and payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 are left exactly as they are.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
